title: Microsoft 365 Backup: dedicated Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator role
summary: The role's permissions, assignment routes, notification controls and activity-log controls are supported by Microsoft documentation. The briefing correctly distinguishes the old roadmap targets from the documented role; minor corrections should acknowledge inconsistent pricing units in Microsoft's pages and remove a checklist instruction not represented in the controls table.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a dedicated Backup Administrator role for Microsoft 365 Backup administration.
claims.quote: Use a dedicated Backup Administrator role to manage your M365 Backup administration tasks.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator is a Microsoft Entra built-in role.
claims.quote:
Microsoft Entra built-in roles
Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator
Assign the Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator role to users who need to do the following tasks:

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The dedicated role permits Backup administration without assigning SharePoint Administrator, Exchange Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: We have also introduced a new dedicated role for this tool, the Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator, that can control the entire tool.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The role is admin-opt-in: its additional privileges take effect when an administrator assigns it.
claims.quote: When you add new users, if you don't assign them an administrator role, they're assigned a user role. Users don't have administrator privileges to any of the Microsoft admin centers.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup uses consumption-based pay-as-you-go entitlement rather than a traditional per-user licence.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup is a pay-as-you-go offering that charges based on consumption, unlike traditional user-based licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Backup pricing page gives a list price of $0.15/GiB/month of protected content.
claims.quote: The list price is $0.15/GiB/month of protected content.
claims.fix: Keep the pricing-page rate and add: 'The overview page still labels its billing unit GB rather than GiB; this briefing uses the pricing page's GiB unit.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-overview alongside https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-pricing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate price for assigning the Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator role.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator role separate licensing price role assignment charge. Opened Backup pricing, overview, setup and billing; read the built-in role reference and assignment guidance. They document protected-content billing, not a separate role-assignment price.
